☕ THE LEAD

Agencies are finally getting real about AI, and it’s about damn time. For the last couple of years, the pitch was all about "efficiency" – faster work, leaner teams, cheaper fees. But clients, bless their hearts, aren't seeing those savings on the invoice, and they're calling BS. Turns out, nobody hires an agency to be *fast*; they hire them to *grow the business*. This week, the conversation is shifting: AI's real power for agencies isn't doing the same work cheaper, it's about delivering better outcomes and creating real value [S10]. Marketers need to stop talking about AI as a cost-cutter and start positioning it as a growth engine. If your agency's AI strategy still sounds like a glorified calculator, you're missing the point (and probably losing clients). The takeaway? If you’re not talking outcomes, you’re just talking. [S5][S10]

📣 QUICK HITS

**Intuit offloads Mailchimp for a fraction of its purchase price.**
Bending Spoons is acquiring the email marketing giant for less than a third of the $12 billion Intuit paid in 2021. This move lets Intuit double down on its AI bets, but wow, that's a tough exit for a brand that was once the darling of small business marketing. [S11]

**A24 releases a "scent score" for its film ‘Backrooms’.**
Joya Studio, known for its fragrance collabs with A24, created five bespoke smells (think: Static, Wet, Yellow) designed to be sprayed at specific timestamps while watching the movie. There's also a candle. Talk about immersive brand extensions! [S16]

**Modelo becomes the first official beer of the NCAA.**
Get ready to see Modelo everywhere from March Madness to over 90 other championships. This is a massive play for brand visibility, strategically aligning with a huge, passionate audience. Expect your sports viewing experience to be extra crisp. [S18]

**Brands are boosting Black Friday digital ad spend by 10-30% this year.**
Retail media (especially Amazon), search, CTV, and YouTube are soaking up most of the increase. While overall holiday marketing tactics are shifting, the big weekend is still a massive digital spend fest. [S26][S29]

🎯 THE PMM DESK

**Kagi Mail launches public beta as a privacy-first email alternative.**
Kagi, already known for its paid search engine and browser, is directly challenging Gmail with Kagi Mail, promising "no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in." It offers 50GB storage and a built-in calendar, with mobile apps slated for Q3 2027. This is a classic "challenger brand" play, leaning heavily into privacy and control as its core differentiator against a market incumbent. [S1]

**Anthropic introduces Claude Ship for AI-powered code review and approval.**
This new offering lets AI agents handle routine approvals and fix code changes, aiming to eliminate bottlenecks in the software development lifecycle. For PMMs, this is a clear example of targeting a specific pain point (developer workflow) with an AI solution, emphasizing efficiency and speed for a technical audience. [S38]

🧠 PMM 101

**The concept:** Value Proposition
What it is: A value proposition is a clear statement that explains what benefits your product or service provides, why it's better than alternatives, and who it's for. It's not just features; it's the *value* those features unlock for a specific customer.
Why it matters: A strong value prop is the foundation of all your marketing and sales efforts, telling customers why they should care.
See it today: Kagi Mail's launch hinges entirely on its value proposition of "no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in" for users fed up with Google's model. They know their target customer and what they value. [S1]
Try it: Pick a product you love. Can you articulate its core value proposition in one sentence? Now, try to do it for a product you *don't* love. What's missing in its message?

🧩 PRODUCT CORNER

**Innovaccer CTO Ankit Maheshwari uses OpenClaw as his personal AI chief of staff.**
Maheshwari runs this system on a Mac Mini, automating everything from work approvals to ordering lunch, calling unresponsive coworkers, booking restaurants, and controlling his smart home. This isn't just a gadget; it's a peek into a future where custom AI agents handle "every 1% annoyance," freeing up executive time for higher-level work. [S6][S7]

🔧 TOOL DROP

The data is a bit thin on new martech/AI/marketing tools today.

⚡ SPEED ROUND

🐶 Pet brands are giving dogs a seat at the Thanksgiving table with new holiday-themed products and campaigns. [S15]
🎥 Uber now offers "Recorded Rides" by default, using the driver's front camera for safety. [S63]
📱 Google Pixel's holiday ad features Dr. Alex Cooper prescribing "less screen time" – a bold move for a phone brand. [S19]
💸 A massive CTV ad fraud scheme, BADBOX 3.0, was uncovered, generating 40 billion fraudulent ad requests daily. Yikes. [S27]
🍎 The Apple Watch Series 12 is hitting new low prices ahead of Black Friday, $100 off at Amazon and Walmart. [S41]
🌳 Meta has quietly ditched its 2030 net-zero goal, drawing criticism from competitors. [S54]
